subject: Materials Science
title: Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion
description: A quick, practical guide to Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion.

hook.text: Bacteria eat sulfate and excrete sulfuric acid — corroding steel pipelines from the inside out.

buildup.text: MIC occurs when microorganisms form biofilms on metal surfaces, creating localized corrosive environments.

discovery.text: Sulfate-reducing bacteria produce hydrogen sulfide under the biofilm — acidifying and pitting the metal.

twist.text: MIC can corrode stainless steel and even titanium — materials normally considered corrosion-proof.

climax.text: Oil pipeline operators use biocides and pigging to remove biofilms before MIC causes catastrophic leaks.

punchline.text: Tiny organisms can eat through the toughest metals — biology vs engineering.

quiz.question: How do sulfate-reducing bacteria cause corrosion?
options: They physically scrape metal from the surface
They produce hydrogen sulfide under biofilms, creating acidic conditions
They consume the metal directly as food
